programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Grumblestunk's new speed camera catches Stan breaking the speed limit on his scooter, but he can't have been! Stan and Gran have to clear his name! Tha an camara luaiths ùr aig Greannarlobht a' glacadh Dan 's e a' briste an casg-astair air an sgùtair aige, ach cha ghabh seo a chreidsinn! Feumaidh Dan is Gran a dhearbhadh neoihiontach!

programme.title: Beathaichean a’ Bocadaich
programme.desc: Tha Sophie a’ coimhead tron phrosbaig sheunta aice airson faicinn ciamar a bhios beathaichean a’ bocadaich. Tha i ag ionnsachadh mar a bhios diofar bheathaichean a’ gluasad agus cuide ri a caraidean, tha i a’ cruthachadh dannsa. An-diugh, danns coltach ri each agus sioraf! Sophie looks through her magic binoculars to find out how animals boogie. She learns how different animals dance and, along with her friends, creates a dance using animal movements. Join her and dance like a horse and a giraffe!

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Tha latha math iasgaich aig na Losgannan agus iad a’ glacadh rud ris nach eil dùil! The Froglets enjoy a fin-tastic fishing adventure, ending up with an unexpected catch!

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha Mamaidh a’ faireachdainn sàraichte is tha i airson ’s gun dèan iad iomlaid len cuid obraichean – gus na tuig iad cho duilich ’s a tha obraichean càch a chèile. Mamaidh is feeling fed up and she wants them all to swap jobs, so they understand how difficult each other’s jobs actually are.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha a’ Chearc Iarainn a’ sealltainn às dèidh na h-oidhcheagan beaga an-diugh ach, mo chreach sa thàinig, abair g’ eil iad ùpraideach! The Iron Chicken is looking after little ones today but, oh my goodness, they are so very noisy!

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Dòmhnall Ruadh a’ leughadh Losgann agus Bìobhar. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Simon James agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill. A bedtime story for young children. Donald Smith reads Losgann agus Bìobhar, written and illustrated by Simon James and translated into Gaelic by Jo Macdonald.

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: Rugadh Hend ann an Ieman ach dh’fhàg i fhèin, a màthair, a piuthar ‘s a bràthair nuair bha i còig, air sgàth a’ chogaidh. Tha i an dòchas bàrdachd a sgrìobhadh gus an ionnsaich an clas mu beatha – ‘s dòcha gun ionnsaich i fhèin rud cuideachd. Hend was born in Yemen but she left with her mother, sister and brother, as a result of the war. She hopes to write poetry so the class will learn about her life - perhaps she will learn something, too.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Chan eil Elaina idir dèidheil air Belle 's tha i ’son coin a bhith toirmisgt’ 'on bhaile. Tha i ag ullachadh reifreann far am bhòt muinntir a’ bhaile le neo an aghaidh Belle, cothrom-inngtrigidh fhaighinn dhan bhaile. Saoil dè thachras? Elaina isn’t fond of Belle and she wants to ban dogs from the village. She organises a referendum where people have to vote for or against Belle being allowed entry to the village. How will it go?

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha a h-uile duine a' coimhead air adhart ri oidhche shàmhach air an tuathanas nuair a tha Bitzer a' fàs an-fhoiseil - chan urrainn dha suidhe aig fois. Nuair a thòisicheas a h-uile duine eile leis an aon ghearan feumaidh Seonaidh faighinn a-mach dè tha ceàrr. Everyone is settling down for a relaxed night on the farm when Bitzer begins to act very strangely - he just can't sit still. When his peculiar behaviour starts spreading around the flock, Shaun decides he must find out what's causing it.

programme.title: A’ Chùil
programme.desc: Tha Choirstaidh air ais le prògram eile bhon stiùidio aice, A’ Chùil. Sa phrògram seo seallaidh i dhut mar a nì thu “Bath Bombs”. Faodaidh tu an toirt seachad mar phrèasantan no faodaidh tu an cumail dhut fhèin! Choirstaidh is back with another programme from her studio A’ Chùil, showing you how to make 'bath bombs'. You can give these as presents or you can keep them for yourself.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Tha Mgr Mackle fo uallach agus chan eil e a’ faighinn fois an àite sam bith. Tha Ms Dallas air a dòigh glan gu bheil An Còirneal Cliseam a' tadhal air an sgoil airson clas air leth a theagaisg. Mr Mackle is under pressure and he can't seem to get any respite. Ms Dallas is delighted that Colonel Clisham is visiting the school to teach a camouflage class.

programme.title: Fuine
programme.desc: Gregor makes chewy and salty bread pretzels that are the perfect snack or lunchbox filler. Griogar MacLeòid is eileanaich eile lem molaidhean son fuine bhlasta staigh agaibh pfhèin

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Humanist celebrant John Howieson chats to Joy in the studio and Calum Maclean is in Lewis, visiting a spiritual site which inspires and amazes.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Rùm Gu Rùm, Le Erica
programme.desc: Tha an cleasaiche, a tha a-nis na dealbhaiche cruthachail thaighean, Erica Mhoireasdan, a’ gabhail sgrìob tron Ghàidhealtachd ‘s na h-Eileanan. Le taic bho luchd-ciùird, tha i a’ lorg dhòighean ùra air seann rumanan a thoirt beò. Actress turned interior designer Erica Morrison takes us on a design adventure throughout the Highlands and Islands. With the help of local craft workers, she finds new ideas for designing old spaces. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Marmalade le Gregor
programme.desc: Agus leis fhèin cho measail air marmalaid, tha Griogar a’ rannsachadh sgeul a’ bhidhe chlasaigeach seo. Marmalade fan Gregor Macleod explores the story of this classic preserve.

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Seata cuirme le Sgoil Chiùil na Gàidhealtachd agus Hadhirgaan, clàraichte beò aig Duaisean nan Trads, 2025. A’ gabhail a-steach Fisherrow Set agus Netherbow Set. Concert set performed by Sgoil Chiùil na Gàidhealtachd and Hadhirgaan, recorded live at the Trad Awards, 2025. Featured tracks include Fisherrow Set and Netherbow Set.

programme.title: Transatlantic Sessions
programme.desc: Julie Fowlis le taghadh ciùil bho dà dheichead den t-sreath-ciùil chliùiteach Transatlantic Sessions. Anns an 7mh prògram de Transatlantic Sessions: Dlùth an Dàimh, ceòl is òrain bho luchd-ciùil às an Rìoghachd Aonaichte, Èirinn agus na Stàitean Aonaichte. Am measg an fheadhainn a cho-obraich agus a tharraing na dùthchannan na bu dlùithe ri cheile, Aly Bain, Alison Krauss, Tim O’ Brien, Dirk Powell & Dónal Lunny. Julie Fowlis presents highlights from two decades of the legendary music show Transatlantic Sessions. This episode has musical stars from the UK, Ireland and the US, including Aly Bain, Alison Krauss, Tim O’ Brien, Dirk Powell and Dónal Lunny.

programme.title: Na Sgiobairean mu Dheireadh/The Last Captains
programme.desc: Tha iasgairean giomach Eileanan Magdalen gan slaiceadh le gèiltean, a’ dèanamh blàr-catha den mhuir far a bheil gach cliabh ag adhbharachadh cunnart. Gale-force winds hammer lobster captains on the Magdalen Islands, turning the sea into a battleground where every trap is a risk. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke head to the woods in search of birch sap, fungi and midgies!

programme.title: Port
programme.desc: Prògram aithriseach ciùil le Julie Fowlis is Muireann NicAmhlaoibh 's iad air slighe rannsachaidh mu na freumhan aca fhèin. Nì iadsan siubhal thar chrìochan 's thar chleachdaidhean eadar taobh siar na h-Èirinn agus Eileanan Siar na h-Alba, a' coinneachadh, a' conaltradh 's a' cluich ciùil air an t-slighe. Chì sinn Julie agus Muireann ann an caochladh àiteachan a tha ainmeil airson òrain, ceòl agus beul-aithris agus a' feitheamh airson fàilte chridheil a chur orra, tha eòlaichean ciùil, pìobairean agus seinneadairean. Anns a' phrògram seo chì sinn stuth nach fhacas a-riamh à Alba agus Èirinn. Musical documentary presented by Julie Fowlis and Muireann NicAmhlaoibh in which they explore their shared musical heritage. Julie and Muireann cross borders and traditions from the Western Isles to the west coast of Ireland, meeting and making music en route. They visit several locations that are synonymous with folk song, music and folklore. Welcoming them to each destination are musicians, pipers and singers, and this episode features previously unseen footage from both Scotland and Ireland.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: She-Wolves: England's Early Queens
programme.desc: In the medieval and Tudor world there was no question in people's minds about the order of God's creation - men ruled and women didn't. A king was a warrior who literally fought to win power then battled to keep it. Yet despite everything that stood in their way, a handful of extraordinary women did attempt to rule medieval and Tudor England. In this series, historian Dr Helen Castor explores seven queens who challenged male power, the fierce reactions they provoked and whether the term 'she wolves' was deserved. Helen looks at what happened when England was faced not just with inadequate kings, but no kings at all. In 1553, for the first time in English history all the contenders for the crown were female. In the lives of these three Tudor queens - Jane, Mary and Elizabeth - she explores how each woman struggled in turn with wearing a crown that was made for a male head. Elizabeth I seemed to show that not only could a woman rule, but could do so gloriously. At what cost though?

programme.title: Castles: Britain's Fortified History
programme.desc: Sam Willis explores how, by the Wars of the Roses, castles were under attack from a new threat - the cannon - but survived into the Tudor era only to find their whole purpose challenged. What had once been strategic seats of power now had to keep up with the fickle fashions of the court and become palaces to impress monarchs such as Elizabeth I. Just as castles seemed to have lost their defensive function, the English Civil War erupted. The legacy of that tumultuous period resulted in castles no longer being associated with protection. Rather, their ruins took on a unique appeal, embodying a nostalgia for an age of chivalry that became a powerful part of the national psyche.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s postwar journey from Merseyside to Teesside resumes at Brayford Pool in Lincoln, where England’s oldest canal, the Fossdyke, meets the city of Lincoln. The larger-than-life figure of one of Britain’s most celebrated poets, Philip Larkin, rushing towards the platform at Hull Paragon Station leads Michael to investigate his life and work. And alongside the Humber estuary, Michael recalls the politics behind the construction of the suspension bridge before making his way to York, one of the host cities for the Festival of Britain in 1951.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s postwar exploration of Merseyside to Teesside finds him in York, a paradise for rail enthusiasts. In the company of some of the most famous locomotives ever built, he recalls the controversy surrounding their relocation from London to a freight depot in York. Michael crosses the magnificent Knaresborough viaduct, with its castellated walls and four beautiful arches over the River Nidd, to reach the spa town of Harrogate. On the edge of the elegant town, Michael discovers the gardens at Harlow Carr and learns how they opened in 1950 to test growing conditions for plants in northern climes. Across town, Michael checks into the headquarters of Yorkshire Tea. And his last destination on this leg of his journey is a bog near Skipton. In the 'gateway to the Dales', he joins members of Yorkshire Peat Partnership to find out what makes a bog.

programme.title: Wainwright Walks
programme.desc: Julia Bradbury sets off to climb her first mountain, Blencathra. Her route to the summit sees her tackle Sharp Edge, the Lake District's most technical and vertigo-inducing ridge climb. In the process, she discovers why the obsessive Wainwright chose to cover this fell in more detail than any other.

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Rome
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke follows in the footsteps of Rome's mad, bad and dangerous emperors in the second part of his celebration of Roman art. He dons a wetsuit to explore the underwater remains of the Emperor Claudius's pleasure palace and ventures into the cave where Tiberius held wild parties. He finds their taste in art chimes perfectly with their obsession with sex and violence. The other side of the coin was the bombastic art the Romans are best remembered for - monumental arches and columns that boast about their conquests. Trajan's Column in Rome reads like the storyboard of a modern-day propaganda film. Sooke concludes with the remarkable legacy of the Emperor Hadrian. He gave the world the magnificent Pantheon in Rome; the eternal image of his lover Antinous - the most beautiful boy in the history of art; and a villa in Tivoli, where he created one of the most ambitious art collections ever assembled.

programme.title: Mary Beard Remembers... Ultimate Rome: Empire Without Limit
programme.desc: Professor Mary Beard is known for her explorations of the ancient world, but here, she looks back on the more recent past and the making of her acclaimed four-part 2016 series Ultimate Rome. Mary explains how the series wasn’t just an education for her in regard to the Roman Empire but also provided valuable lessons in the art of film-making. She reveals some behind-the-scenes stories that add new context for viewers of the main episodes. They include the importance of pizza and how Mary's claim to be the first to wear an antique Roman helmet was way off the mark.

programme.title: Mary Beard's Ultimate Rome: Empire Without Limit
programme.desc: Mary Beard takes in the mythology, history and archaeology of Rome. In the first episode, Mary reaches back to the myths and legends of the origins of Rome.

programme.desc: Livia engineers the downfall of Julia, who is banished. Tiberius is recalled to Rome and is joint heir with Postumus. Poor stumbling, stuttering Claudius finds a friend in Herod, king of the Jews.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: The keepers are deeply concerned about Klaus, one of the park’s most impressive lions. A stubborn paw injury has left him limping and reluctant to move. Fearing that the infection could worsen, the decision is made to sedate him for urgent treatment. But at nearly 18 years old, the procedure carries a serious risk, so the team must work fast to investigate the wound and bring him round. Meanwhile, Megan plays a game with Anne the elephant, Kate confronts her fear of spiders, and Hamza successfully captures footage of the white-backed vulture chick.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: In Birmingham, a family’s much-loved motorhome is stolen off their driveway. There is dramatic CCTV footage of the theft – but incidents like this are increasingly common. Meanwhile, tracker Richard is searching for a vehicle worth £40,000 that was stolen from a builders’ yard in south west London - but it’s a race against time. There is a high demand for construction vehicles like this in countries like Ukraine, and thieves are cashing in. Richard suspects it could be about to be shipped overseas. In the UK’s biggest cities, organised gangs of thieves are targeting electric bikes worth thousands of pounds. Bike recovery specialist Bilal is hunting down a stolen e-bike that is fitted with a tracker and has a child’s seat on the back. As a father himself, Bilal is determined to get the bike back. The tracker’s GPS signal is being affected by the number of tall buildings in the area, so he deploys a drone to help with the search.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: When a young man is stabbed to death, a facial recognition expert helps Merseyside Police catch the killer. And a specialist palynologist’s help is needed by detectives investigating the disappearance of an elderly couple.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martel, Jacqui and Owain are across the UK, checking out no less than four flats in Scotland, England and Wales! All are in a poor state of repair, and all are transformed, adding new kitchens, bathrooms and extra bedrooms in the hope of adding profit too.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion is in Wrexham, where the red and blue teams are guided around the antiques centre by experts Jonathan Pratt and Tim Weeks. Then it is off to the auction in Dudley. Meanwhile, Christina finds out about the history of Chester silver and why it is so desirable to bargain hunters.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Are creative curves good for us? Katie and Sophie attempt a wavy redesign that leaves them feeling seasick, and woodworker Bruce is pushed to his limits trying to rejuvenate a pair of old, dated desk ends. Meanwhile, Sarah Moore attempts to trick the eye by updating a display cabinet – but will all three revamps produce profits?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Sonali Shah tours the East Midlands in search of a property to suit today’s buyers who, for the last 23 years, have been living in the USA. Sonali also meets another couple who relocated from America and set about renovating their gorgeous Leicestershire home, parts of which date back to the 18th century.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.desc: Can today’s teams tell Emmerdale from Coronation Street, Twickenham from Wembley, and Tom Hanks from Tom Cruise? Jason Manford hosts the quiz where every answer is a choice and every choice counts.

programme.title: You're Cordially Invited
programme.desc: When two weddings are accidentally booked on the same day at the same venue, each bridal party is challenged with preserving their family’s special moment while making the most of the unanticipated tight quarters. In a battle of determination and grit, the father of one bride and the sister of the other bride chaotically go head-to-head as they stop at nothing to uphold an unforgettable celebration for their loved ones. Save the date, prepare for chaos. Comedy.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: In Birmingham, a family’s much-loved motorhome is stolen off their driveway. There is dramatic CCTV footage of the theft – but incidents like this are increasingly common. Meanwhile, tracker Richard is searching for a vehicle worth £40,000 that was stolen from a builders’ yard in south west London - but it’s a race against time. There is a high demand for construction vehicles like this in countries like Ukraine, and thieves are cashing in. Richard suspects it could be about to be shipped overseas. In the UK’s biggest cities, organised gangs of thieves are targeting electric bikes worth thousands of pounds. Bike recovery specialist Bilal is hunting down a stolen e-bike that is fitted with a tracker and has a child’s seat on the back. As a father himself, Bilal is determined to get the bike back. The tracker’s GPS signal is being affected by the number of tall buildings in the area, so he deploys a drone to help with the search.

programme.title: Breakfast

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: The keepers are deeply concerned about Klaus, one of the park’s most impressive lions. A stubborn paw injury has left him limping and reluctant to move. Fearing that the infection could worsen, the decision is made to sedate him for urgent treatment. But at nearly 18 years old, the procedure carries a serious risk, so the team must work fast to investigate the wound and bring him round. Meanwhile, Megan plays a game with Anne the elephant, Kate confronts her fear of spiders, and Hamza successfully captures footage of the white-backed vulture chick.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: In Birmingham, a family’s much-loved motorhome is stolen off their driveway. There is dramatic CCTV footage of the theft – but incidents like this are increasingly common. Meanwhile, tracker Richard is searching for a vehicle worth £40,000 that was stolen from a builders’ yard in south west London - but it’s a race against time. There is a high demand for construction vehicles like this in countries like Ukraine, and thieves are cashing in. Richard suspects it could be about to be shipped overseas. In the UK’s biggest cities, organised gangs of thieves are targeting electric bikes worth thousands of pounds. Bike recovery specialist Bilal is hunting down a stolen e-bike that is fitted with a tracker and has a child’s seat on the back. As a father himself, Bilal is determined to get the bike back. The tracker’s GPS signal is being affected by the number of tall buildings in the area, so he deploys a drone to help with the search.

programme.desc: When a young man is stabbed to death, a facial recognition expert helps Merseyside Police catch the killer. And a specialist palynologist’s help is needed by detectives investigating the disappearance of an elderly couple.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion is in Wrexham, where the red and blue teams are guided around the antiques centre by experts Jonathan Pratt and Tim Weeks. Then it is off to the auction in Dudley. programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Sonali Shah tours the East Midlands in search of a property to suit today’s buyers who, for the last 23 years, have been living in the USA. programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: The keepers are deeply concerned about Klaus, one of the park’s most impressive lions. A stubborn paw injury has left him limping and reluctant to move. Fearing that the infection could worsen, the decision is made to sedate him for urgent treatment. But at nearly 18 years old, the procedure carries a serious risk, so the team must work fast to investigate the wound and bring him round. Meanwhile, Megan plays a game with Anne the elephant, Kate confronts her fear of spiders, and Hamza successfully captures footage of the white-backed vulture chick.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: In Birmingham, a family’s much-loved motorhome is stolen off their driveway. There is dramatic CCTV footage of the theft – but incidents like this are increasingly common. Meanwhile, tracker Richard is searching for a vehicle worth £40,000 that was stolen from a builders’ yard in south west London - but it’s a race against time. There is a high demand for construction vehicles like this in countries like Ukraine, and thieves are cashing in. Richard suspects it could be about to be shipped overseas. In the UK’s biggest cities, organised gangs of thieves are targeting electric bikes worth thousands of pounds. Bike recovery specialist Bilal is hunting down a stolen e-bike that is fitted with a tracker and has a child’s seat on the back. As a father himself, Bilal is determined to get the bike back. The tracker’s GPS signal is being affected by the number of tall buildings in the area, so he deploys a drone to help with the search.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: When a young man is stabbed to death, a facial recognition expert helps Merseyside Police catch the killer. And a specialist palynologist’s help is needed by detectives investigating the disappearance of an elderly couple.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martel, Jacqui and Owain are across the UK, checking out no less than four flats in Scotland, England and Wales! All are in a poor state of repair, and all are transformed, adding new kitchens, bathrooms and extra bedrooms in the hope of adding profit too.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion is in Wrexham, where the red and blue teams are guided around the antiques centre by experts Jonathan Pratt and Tim Weeks. Then it is off to the auction in Dudley. Meanwhile, Christina finds out about the history of Chester silver and why it is so desirable to bargain hunters.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Sonali Shah tours the East Midlands in search of a property to suit today’s buyers who, for the last 23 years, have been living in the USA. programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Former miner Peter Lawson is the beating heart of Durham’s Easington Colliery Band. He joined the band at 11 and has worked tirelessly for 55 years to keep it going. From managing the band, to moving equipment and raising money with a band cafe, the list is endless. His dedication has seen the band grow and in 2024 win the North of England Championships. Last year, they also performed with music legend Sam Fender. Seventy-five years ago, the mining community suffered one of the north east’s worst pit disasters. The band united the community and played at every one of funerals of the 83 men that died. To mark the anniversary, the band is preparing for their biggest concert at Durham Cathedral. Teacher Dan is busy recruiting new band members to play, and local children are rehearsing their contribution, A Miner’s Song, so that it can be ready for the concert. But with Peter unwell with what could be a serious condition, and Dan and Georgia expecting a baby the week of the concert, will the key members of the band be there? And if Peter retires, what happens to the band? Will the next generation step up to the challenge?

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: The keepers are deeply concerned about Klaus, one of the park’s most impressive lions. A stubborn paw injury has left him limping and reluctant to move. Fearing that the infection could worsen, the decision is made to sedate him for urgent treatment. But at nearly 18 years old, the procedure carries a serious risk, so the team must work fast to investigate the wound and bring him round. Meanwhile, Megan plays a game with Anne the elephant, Kate confronts her fear of spiders, and Hamza successfully captures footage of the white-backed vulture chick.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: In Birmingham, a family’s much-loved motorhome is stolen off their driveway. There is dramatic CCTV footage of the theft – but incidents like this are increasingly common. Meanwhile, tracker Richard is searching for a vehicle worth £40,000 that was stolen from a builders’ yard in south west London - but it’s a race against time. There is a high demand for construction vehicles like this in countries like Ukraine, and thieves are cashing in. Richard suspects it could be about to be shipped overseas. In the UK’s biggest cities, organised gangs of thieves are targeting electric bikes worth thousands of pounds. Bike recovery specialist Bilal is hunting down a stolen e-bike that is fitted with a tracker and has a child’s seat on the back. As a father himself, Bilal is determined to get the bike back. The tracker’s GPS signal is being affected by the number of tall buildings in the area, so he deploys a drone to help with the search.

programme.title: The Hit List
programme.desc: It’s a star-studded celebrity special as Marvin and Rochelle welcome six famous faces to battle it out for charity. programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: The keepers are deeply concerned about Klaus, one of the park’s most impressive lions. A stubborn paw injury has left him limping and reluctant to move. Fearing that the infection could worsen, the decision is made to sedate him for urgent treatment. But at nearly 18 years old, the procedure carries a serious risk, so the team must work fast to investigate the wound and bring him round. Meanwhile, Megan plays a game with Anne the elephant, Kate confronts her fear of spiders, and Hamza successfully captures footage of the white-backed vulture chick.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: In Birmingham, a family’s much-loved motorhome is stolen off their driveway. There is dramatic CCTV footage of the theft – but incidents like this are increasingly common. Meanwhile, tracker Richard is searching for a vehicle worth £40,000 that was stolen from a builders’ yard in south west London - but it’s a race against time. There is a high demand for construction vehicles like this in countries like Ukraine, and thieves are cashing in. Richard suspects it could be about to be shipped overseas. In the UK’s biggest cities, organised gangs of thieves are targeting electric bikes worth thousands of pounds. Bike recovery specialist Bilal is hunting down a stolen e-bike that is fitted with a tracker and has a child’s seat on the back. As a father himself, Bilal is determined to get the bike back. The tracker’s GPS signal is being affected by the number of tall buildings in the area, so he deploys a drone to help with the search.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: When a young man is stabbed to death, a facial recognition expert helps Merseyside Police catch the killer. And a specialist palynologist’s help is needed by detectives investigating the disappearance of an elderly couple.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martel, Jacqui and Owain are across the UK, checking out no less than four flats in Scotland, England and Wales! All are in a poor state of repair, and all are transformed, adding new kitchens, bathrooms and extra bedrooms in the hope of adding profit too.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion is in Wrexham, where the red and blue teams are guided around the antiques centre by experts Jonathan Pratt and Tim Weeks. Then it is off to the auction in Dudley. Meanwhile, Christina finds out about the history of Chester silver and why it is so desirable to bargain hunters.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Are creative curves good for us? programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Sonali Shah tours the East Midlands in search of a property to suit today’s buyers who, for the last 23 years, have been living in the USA. programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Deep in the waters of the Indian Ocean, Steve goes in search of the biggest fish in the sea, so big that it can weigh as much as a double decker bus. He also goes looking for the fastest fish on the planet, but travelling at speeds of 80 miles per hour, Steve's got his work cut out. After an encounter with a starfish that kills coral with lethal stomach juices, the crew's nerves are tested to their limit when a truly scary animal turns up uninvited at their digs back on dry land.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: With his crew in tow, Steve is on a mission to find all the animals that most Africans spend as much time as possible avoiding. Steve braves the big waves of the Durban coast to get up close and personal with a pack of 30 hungry blacktip sharks, getting a bit too close for comfort. After swimming in shark-infested waters, Steve abseils down to a nest of killer bees with a painful outcome. An eerily close encounter with a ragged tooth shark is followed by getting airborne with the awesome black eagle. Unlike Rourke the eagle, Steve comes down to earth with a bump.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May are challenged to knock down a row of derelict houses in less time than it takes a team of demolition experts to do the same job. Jeremy tests an updated version of the classic Jensen Interceptor and finds himself transported back to a 1970s world of leather driving gloves and droopy moustaches. The show also features the Lotus T125 which brings F1-style performance to the track, plus another celebrity guest attempts a record lap in the Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May embark on a grand road trip across Australia's Northern Territory. Tasked with picking a fast, luxurious GT for the trip, Clarkson chooses a BMW M6 Gran Coupe, Hammond a Bentley Continental GT V8 and May a Nissan GT-R, as the trio set out on an adventure that takes in crocodile-infested rivers, a race around a vast open-cast mine, an encounter with the world's longest lorries and the majestic scenery of one of the world's least-inhabited landscapes. Their dusty endeavour concludes with an unusual challenge involving a farm, their cars and 4,000 cows. Also in this episode, Hollywood legend Kiefer Sutherland is the star in the Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: Guy Montgomery’s Guy Mont-Spelling Bee Australia
programme.desc: Hannah Gadsby and Lloyd Langford join a panel of comedians taking on TV’s silliest spelling test. Only one will snag a winning ticket to the next episode.

programme.title: Guy Montgomery’s Guy Mont-Spelling Bee Australia
programme.desc: Loves is in the air as Hannah Gadsby takes on a fresh panel of comedians to spell their way through a dating round, before Farmer Aaron leads a rural spelling challenge.

programme.title: Dinosaur
programme.desc: Nina is happy in her world, but when her best friend and sister Evie delivers some news, she realises everything is going to change. However, this isn’t the only upheaval coming Nina’s way.

programme.title: Dinosaur
programme.desc: Nina and Evie hatch a plan to impress Ranesh’s intimidating dad, Sachin. They must win him over before they share the news of Evie and Ranesh’s engagement.

programme.title: Dinosaur
programme.desc: It’s a turbulent day for Nina: her first date with Lee is derailed when Evie plans her bridesmaid’s dress fitting in the middle of it.

programme.title: Jesy Nelson: 'Odd One Out'
programme.desc: When Jesy Nelson rose to fame with pop band Little Mix, she was abused online for being 'the fat one'. Now, for the first time, she opens up about the heartbreaking effects cyberbullies have had on her life. In this intimate, personal documentary, Jesy exclusively reveals the impact online trolls had on her mental health as she goes on a journey of rehabilitation. Allowing cameras a behind-the-scenes look at her personal and professional life, Jesy begins to understand the layers of protection she has built in order to cope with the bullies. To help her heal, she meets other victims of cyber abuse, sharing devastating stories of online trolling. Little Mix members Perrie, Leigh-Anne and Jade discuss how Jesy’s torment affected the dynamics within the band and how it impacted the group’s ability to perform. Jesy’s boyfriend, Love Island star Chris Hughes, offers a comforting support system to the pop star. He recounts falling in love with someone who was clearly damaged by the barrage of negativity she experienced on social media. And members of Jesy’s family help her confront deep personal issues she's kept hidden for years.

programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: JJ Chalmers is on patrol at Dunfermline recycling centre, hoping to uncover three lucrative items amongst the skip-bound trash. Blacksmith Kev creates a metal masterpiece from obsolete tools, while JJ tries to double the charm of two rattan chairs. JJ hands over a huge profit, but which upcycled find will generate the most cash?

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Boarding the superfast Shinkansen bullet train, Michael heads north from Tokyo to Honshu’s Tohoku region, known as the rice granary of Japan. He visits a fifth-generation rice farm to discover how the crop is cultivated and processed, and takes a turn around the field on a combine harvester. Continuing his route north, Michael’s next stop is the city of Sendai. He learns how disaster struck in March 2011, when the coast was hit by a powerful earthquake and a devastating tsunami. On the roof of a primary school in the neighbourhood of Arahama, which overlooks the beach, the former principal shares his powerful memories of the fateful day and his plan to save his pupils. Further up the coast at the fishing port of Shiogama, Michael attends the daily tuna auction and watches as bidders compete for the prized fish, with the largest fetching almost £1,900. The town boasts more sushi restaurants per capita than anywhere in the country, and Michael enjoys a tasting with a master chef.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his Sardinian railway adventure, arriving in Mamoiada to investigate the town’s extraordinary pagan traditions. In a menacing mask, black sheepskin and 30 kg of cowbells, Michael embraces the role of a mamuthone, who wards off evil spirits. Taking a 1950s diesel railcar, Michael journeys across the island to Macomer, where he discovers the railway’s surprising connection to a pioneering Welsh railway engineer. His adventure concludes at Italy’s largest cork factory, where a team of expert sniffers safeguard the integrity of the world’s finest wines.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Sean Fletcher, Louise Minchin, Chris Washington and Kimberly Wyatt take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Halfway through the week, TV icon Anneka Rice, comedian Shane Todd and Radio 1Xtra DJ Remi Burgz face a fresh test of knowledge. Vernon Kay puts the spotlight onto his home town of Bolton, while unreliable guide Paul Gorton delivers the tour, complete with a few extra treats along the way.

programme.title: Cricket: The Hundred
programme.desc: Coverage of The Hundred 100-ball cricket tournament.

programme.title: Cricket: The Hundred
programme.desc: Coverage of The Hundred 100-ball cricket tournament.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: Ria Lina introduces comedians Lucy Beaumont and Josh Pugh to the stage.

programme.title: The Big Cases
programme.desc: The chilling story of Hull’s funeral home horror. How an undertaker drowning in debt betrayed hundreds of grieving families. Robert Bush hoarded bodies, sold fake funeral plans and presented families with the ashes of strangers. His shocking crimes went undetected for years. The discovery led to one of the most complex investigations in Humberside Police’s history, with help from the National Crime Agency. At the heart of this are grieving families. In their darkest days, they fought for laws to regulate the funeral industry so that others never suffer their pain - or guilt - again.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Uncanny
programme.desc: It’s the early 1990s, and while many students their age are out raving, three theology students at Oxford University are about to experience the house share from hell... In this third and final case, Danny Robins meets Heather, who, 30 years ago, moves into a student house with two friends – a house which they believe is haunted by a malevolent entity. Events become so frightening that the group are compelled to call in an exorcist - but the exorcism doesn’t go according to plan. It’s one of the most unsettling cases Danny has ever come across. But could it simply be a shared delusion? To find an answer, Danny must track down Heather’s housemates to find out what they remember about the events. Assisting him in his search for answers are Dr Ciarán O’Keeffe and parapsychologist Evelyn Hollow.

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke
programme.desc: Ruby and Jodi’s partnership deepens as together they reshape the family, and Ruby starts to banish members of the family from their home.

programme.title: Amityville: An Origin Story
programme.desc: A year before the Lutzes move into 112 Ocean Ave, the DeFeo family is found shot to death under strange circumstances in the same house. The lone survivor, Ronnie DeFeo Jr, is accused of murder, but mob ties and paranormal theories cloud the case.

Events become so frightening that the group are compelled to call in an exorcist - but the exorcism doesn’t go according to plan. It’s one of the most unsettling cases Danny has ever come across. But could it simply be a shared delusion? To find an answer, Danny must track down Heather’s housemates to find out what they remember about the events. Assisting him in his search for answers are Dr Ciarán O’Keeffe and parapsychologist Evelyn Hollow.

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke

programme.title: Amityville: An Origin Story
programme.desc: A year before the Lutzes move into 112 Ocean Ave, the DeFeo family is found shot to death under strange circumstances in the same house. The lone survivor, Ronnie DeFeo Jr, is accused of murder, but mob ties and paranormal theories cloud the case.

programme.title: Uncanny
programme.desc: Was a young girl in rural Cambridgeshire visited by the apparition of an Edwardian school teacher? programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: JJ Chalmers is on patrol at Dunfermline recycling centre, hoping to uncover three lucrative items amongst the skip-bound trash. Blacksmith Kev creates a metal masterpiece from obsolete tools, while JJ tries to double the charm of two rattan chairs. JJ hands over a huge profit, but which upcycled find will generate the most cash?

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Boarding the superfast Shinkansen bullet train, Michael heads north from Tokyo to Honshu’s Tohoku region, known as the rice granary of Japan. He visits a fifth-generation rice farm to discover how the crop is cultivated and processed, and takes a turn around the field on a combine harvester. Continuing his route north, Michael’s next stop is the city of Sendai. He learns how disaster struck in March 2011, when the coast was hit by a powerful earthquake and a devastating tsunami. On the roof of a primary school in the neighbourhood of Arahama, which overlooks the beach, the former principal shares his powerful memories of the fateful day and his plan to save his pupils. Further up the coast at the fishing port of Shiogama, Michael attends the daily tuna auction and watches as bidders compete for the prized fish, with the largest fetching almost £1,900. The town boasts more sushi restaurants per capita than anywhere in the country, and Michael enjoys a tasting with a master chef.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his Sardinian railway adventure, arriving in Mamoiada to investigate the town’s extraordinary pagan traditions. In a menacing mask, black sheepskin and 30 kg of cowbells, Michael embraces the role of a mamuthone, who wards off evil spirits. Taking a 1950s diesel railcar, Michael journeys across the island to Macomer, where he discovers the railway’s surprising connection to a pioneering Welsh railway engineer. His adventure concludes at Italy’s largest cork factory, where a team of expert sniffers safeguard the integrity of the world’s finest wines.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi, Dash and Jake set off on a camping adventure, determined to stick to their wizarding scout plan - no wishes allowed! When they realise the original plan won’t work, Rafi suggests making a new one instead. With teamwork, flexibility and the right wish, the Wizard Wagon takes flight and carries them to the perfect camping spot at sunset. Rafi learns that plans can change, and sometimes the best adventures come from making a new one together.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran are planning on baking a sweet banana loaf for Jared, who’s coming to Gran Gran’s house for dinner. But as they get the ingredients ready, Gran Gran realises the bananas are still green, which means they can’t make a sweet loaf. Great-Gran Gran shares another green recipe – a tomato salad. Maybe there’s another Caribbean dish with unripe bananas that JoJo can make for Jared.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Sarah is a seven-year-old girl with big eyes and a green hat, who lives with her quacky, flappy, slightly manic but endearing best friend Duck. The pair embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. After Sarah helps Scarf Lady prepare the wool for her new roof, she settles down for a dreamy sleep.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Small gives Tiny a lovely sparkly bag which he has caught when fishing in space. It is perfect for Tiny's panpipes. But when she goes to get her panpipes out of the bag, she is amazed to find it speaks, in sounds and shapes.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa play tickle chase with a Tweetie feather. At Play Time, they choose to play with a feather duster, aka a tickle wand! MeMo chases BaBa with the wand. It is fun at first, but then BaBa wants to stop playing.

programme.desc: The Squirrels are helping Duggee in the garden when Tag makes friends with a caterpillar. This caterpillar is very hungry, so Tag feeds her all the vegetable leaves they have been picking. She eats and eats and eats and gets bigger and bigger. Wow! The other Squirrels are really keen to play with her too, but Tag's caterpillar friend is suddenly very tired and needs to sleep. The Squirrels are also a bit sleepy, time for a nap! When the Squirrels wake up, they cannot find caterpillar - she has disappeared. In her place, as if by magic, there is someone else. How did that happen?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: It's lovely and warm - just right for a day on the beach. The Squirrels learn how to make sandcastles - dig, dig, dig! They are doing such a good job that Jon and Nigel ask the crabs if the Squirrels could work together to build them a new home. They create the most spectacular giant sandcastle ever seen, with shells, seaweed, great views and lots of sand.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: When Mum’s sister Brandy comes over for a visit, she brings Bluey and Bingo onesies.

programme.title: Bluey

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Grandmaster Glitch is late for the European Moustache of the Year award ceremony, and even worse, he's broken down! The Grimbots are on hand to recommend a shortcut: the Panama Canal, a man-made passage that provides a gateway between the Pacific and Atlantic oceans. Meanwhile, the Go Jetters are also heading to the Panama Canal to see its huge watery steps in action, but they arrive to find honking ships' horns and a huge traffic jam - it's all been glitched! In an attempt to jump the queue of ships, Glitch has jammed the canal doors open. Not only is the canal flooding and the other ships unable to get through, but Grim HQ and Grandmaster Glitch are sinking. With the Grimbots busy with their rubber ducks, it's down to the Go Jetters to save the day.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Sammy Whiskers dupes three innocent mice into stealing the rabbits' plum pie, Peter must rescue both pie and mice from the clutches of Mr Tod.

programme.title: Numberblocks

programme.title: Alphablocks

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: The Piris must find a solution when a flock of hungry seagulls nearly capsize the iceberg. Can Pancake’s rare, smelly seaweed help them get rid of the unwanted guests and save the day?

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Pearl accidentally gives Fizz and Zog a laughing disease called the draggles. The doctors must create an emotion potion before every dragon chuckles themselves to exhaustion.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Tao needs help learning to fly his new wingsuit for a big town event, and Mojo and Bo are the experts. Can they help him find his inner bird before it’s too late?

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: It's vaccination day! Bing knows it might hurt a little but he is looking forward to the special shiny Hoppity Voosh sticker he will get from Doctor Molly. Bing is brave, but when he goes to get his sticker after his vaccination, he finds out that there are none left! Bing is upset - but then Pando mistakes Bing's disappointment for pain, and Doctor Bing has to help.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘hand’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We see shaking, making and baking hands. We wash our hands, reach high with them, and Dee waves goodbye with her hand! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie is unsure about giving away her old xylophone, and playing the very first melody she ever wrote brings back lots of feelings. But when she hears the instrument bringing joy to a little girl, Maddie soon knows what she needs to do.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Fred and Dana's door makes a squeaky sound, so they call the Piggy Builders to fix it. The Piggies decide to upgrade the entire door. They build the greatest door ever, but then forget how to open it.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are stroking a lady's soft, fluffy hat. Toodloo runs off underneath the hat and Great BigHoo, Chickedy and Chick chase after it. A lady walking her dog strokes the hat, a man eating his sandwiches accidentally tries to eat it and a bald man enjoys wearing it. A soft sea sponge comes out of Peekaboo's house with Peekaboo snuggled inside. The Twirlywoos come back to the Big Red Boat and the sponge rolls in past them. Chickedy and Chick snuggle into the sponge. Toodloo strokes the sponge and it jumps on her head. Peekaboo tries to get the sponge back to his house but Great BigHoo chases after them. The soft sponge wraps itself around Great BigHoo's body. Peekaboo calls the sponge back to his house so he can snuggle back into it.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: There's make-believe fun for Justin and his friend as they pretend to run a pizza restaurant. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble is knitting a fancy new jumper to wear for his pretend fashion show.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Po gets on the Tubby Custard Ride and makes lots of tubby custard - far too much for Po to eat alone! Po choo-choos off to find Tinky Winky, Dipsy and Laa-Laa so all the Teletubbies can share in the tubby custard. In Tummy Tales, the children take a ride on a steam train.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Layla, George, Isobel, Lincoln, Jason, Willow and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are different types of Paper, which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding safe, baby appropriate paper inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun song ‘Colourful Paper’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: I Spy, You Spy
programme.desc: Elsee plays I-spy with her friend Bailey in his back garden.

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: Botanist Matilda and the Fact Pack explore the incredible Wollemi pine, a prehistoric plant from the time of the dinosaurs. They have fun making their own Wollemi pine fossils.

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk to the park to have a picnic. On the way they tip-toe past a sleeping snake at the city walls, taste some bread in the market and make some silly faces!

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri wakes up one morning to find all her friends have disappeared.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: While away camping, Bluey makes a new friend called Jean-Luc. Despite speaking different languages, they come up with a great game. Bluey is sad when Jean-Luc goes home unexpectedly but learns that even if friendships are fleeting they can still mean a lot.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Join Duggee, a big, lovable dog, as he runs the Squirrel Club, where children can earn badges for learning new skills. Warm-hearted preschool series about trying new things.

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Today, Himmat wants to learn about wonderful woodlice! Rory and his son Sandy go hunting for woodlice in the park and build a bug hotel, while Ferne learns that woodlice are crustaceans just like crayfish. Plus, we find out how woodlice are great for the environment – they are little eco-engineers!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Amanpreet and her family are off on a animal adventure! They visit a safari park where they join the lions for a spot of lunch from the safety of their safari bus. Later, Amanpreet turns her hand to zookeeping. The rhino’s need a mud bath and Amanpreet is ready to help - it’s a mucky job, but someone has to do it! She also gets to feed the giraffes, but will the gentle giants be tempted by her cabbage buffet?

programme.title: Big Cook Little Cook
programme.desc: Children’s cookery series with Big Cook Jen and Little Cook Small. Small has a new recorder, but is having trouble learning how to play it. Jen and Small cook the Pied Piper something tasty and tuneful.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Dan and Jamie ride the chairlift to the top of the mountain to warn some hikers that the resort is closing because of a storm. Can they get everyone off the mountain safely in time?

programme.title: Time for School
programme.desc: The class has a visit from Karen, the dental nurse, who shows them how to keep their teeth clean. She asks Jud to be a pretend dentist and give Oliver’s teeth a check-over, but how many teeth does he have? Jud, Oliver and Jessica are then given the chance to practise their brushing skills with Karen. She gives them some top tips to make sure they always have gleaming white smiles. Solomon is in the dental surgery role play area. First, it’s his turn to be a dentist and Mrs Hussain is the patient, then they swap roles. After lunch, Mrs Farrell and the children try out the skills they’ve learnt by giving their teeth a brush.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Bernie is washed out to sea on a bit of driftwood while waiting on Bernadette for a date. Oona tries her best to help, but the driftwood is too heavy. They need help from a good swimmer, so Oona goes in search of Marvin the otter. She has to be quick - the tide is going out and carrying Bernie further away, but Marvin is nowhere to be found!

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Sonny finds an old musical safe, which only opens with the right musical code. With Yukee’s help, Sonny tries every tune he can think of, but none opens the box – until the answer appears in a very unexpected place!

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs are off to the bowling alley with Mum and Dad. Everyone else is knocking down pins, but poor Dad just can’t catch a break. Time to focus! Can Maddie and Triggs help Dad find his bowling groove and get that elusive strike, or will he be left in the gutter?

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: The Piggies take on multiple missions and decide to split up. They soon realise they were all working on Fiona’s surprise birthday! Nothing is ready... Mission impossible? Not if they join forces!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Meet the really big square who always gets the party started: Sixteen! Learn all about the number 16 with Numberblock Sixteen.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: When the Alphablocks go on holiday, a trip on a train is the only way to travel - if only the train would travel somewhere! This episode introduces the '-ai-' digraph and the words rail, rain, train, wait, chain, fail and sail.

programme.desc: Justin spends the day at his friend's school. They have lots of fun in the classroom, meeting the school dog and eating pizza. Meanwhile, it is Tumble Ted's first day at school and Mr Tumble pretends to be the teacher.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Teletubbies say 'eh-oh' to each other in turn and then say 'eh-oh' to flowers, while the children in Tummy Tales make a friendship circle out of handprints.

At the end of the day, Mack teases Molly for giving away all of his medals, but he has to admit that everyone did deserve them.

Dodge realises he has to take responsibility and do the job himself.

programme.title: The Summit
programme.desc: Ben Shephard presents the thrilling reality series where 14 ordinary Brits climb one of New Zealand's highest peaks to win a share of 200,000 pounds. The fallout from the brutal bridge chop, which saw the mountain claim its first victim, is still simmering as construction manager Dockers is singled out as a game-player and not to be trusted - to succeed on their journey, the group must put differences aside and pull together as they endure a gruelling eight-hour uphill hike while carrying their share of the prize money on their backs. If they quit, their share of the money will be lost - as pub landlady Miranda and football coach Tyra struggle to keep up, Afton - a daughter of celebrity nutritionist Gillian McKeith - has her attitude called into question while a terrifying ladder climb sees influencer Patrick under pressure as his over-confidence gets the better of him. The Mountain's Keeper, who is tracking the group's every move, then presents them with another difficult dilemma...

programme.title: Long Lost Family: Born Without Trace
programme.desc: August 1983: a newborn baby is found, wrapped only in a towel, in a public phone box in Leicester. Now 41 and a mother herself, Sarah wants to know whether it was her own mother who left her there, and if so, why? 1960: a baby boy, warmly dressed and wrapped, is discovered on the second floor of a locked London mansion block. As so often with these extraordinary foundling stories, the answers produce tears of both heartbreak and joy.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: Long Lost Family: Born Without Trace
programme.desc: August 1983: a newborn baby is found, wrapped only in a towel, in a public phone box in Leicester. programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: Long Lost Family: Born Without Trace
programme.desc: August 1983: a newborn baby is found, wrapped only in a towel, in a public phone box in Leicester. Now 41 and a mother herself, Sarah wants to know whether it was her own mother who left her there, and if so, why? 1960: a baby boy, warmly dressed and wrapped, is discovered on the second floor of a locked London mansion block. As so often with these extraordinary foundling stories, the answers produce tears of both heartbreak and joy.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.title: The Summit
programme.desc: Ben Shephard presents the thrilling reality series where 14 ordinary Brits climb one of New Zealand's highest peaks to win a share of 200,000 pounds. The fallout from the brutal bridge chop, which saw the mountain claim its first victim, is still simmering as construction manager Dockers is singled out as a game-player and not to be trusted - to succeed on their journey, the group must put differences aside and pull together as they endure a gruelling eight-hour uphill hike while carrying their share of the prize money on their backs. If they quit, their share of the money will be lost - as pub landlady Miranda and football coach Tyra struggle to keep up, Afton - a daughter of celebrity nutritionist Gillian McKeith - has her attitude called into question while a terrifying ladder climb sees influencer Patrick under pressure as his over-confidence gets the better of him. The Mountain's Keeper, who is tracking the group's every move, then presents them with another difficult dilemma...

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Aitch faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. What's his PIN number? How much does his watch cost? What's so good about Manchester? From the moment he enters the room, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Aitch reflects on his lyrics and the language he used early in his career, admitting he felt pressure to say certain things as a young rapper - and that he got it wrong. He opens up about fame, identity and the nuances of being a white rapper in a typically black scene, as well as the values that matter most to him now. Along the way, there are questions about first dates and apologies, with time for a tour of his tattoos and the story of standing up for his sister. In a deeply moving moment, he shares what he hopes for her future, and admits he's still figuring out how to calm his mind when things feel overwhelming. From big laughs to real vulnerability, this is Aitch as you've never seen him before.

programme.desc: Londoner Frankie is hoping to find her dream man. Which of the three single men shopping for her will impress her enough to win a date?

programme.desc: US reality series peeking inside the unconventional lives of six successful women living in or around Salt Lake City, Utah. The Santorini trip continues. programme.title: The Real Housewives of Orange County
programme.desc: Reality show following the lavish lifestyles of five 'housewives' and their families. Tamra decides to give herself some space from Gretchen, Emily and Shane are more in sync after receiving a diagnosis for Luke, and Jenn expresses her concerns as Dawson preps to leave for the Marines - Tamra then throws a Spring Fling party, but the evening devolves into chaos when careers, trust and betrayals come into question.

programme.title: The Only Way is Essex
programme.desc: Essex is a small place, and Dani knew it was only a matter of time before she would have to come face to face with the Great Gatsby now he is back from LA - will they have an amicable first meet when the time comes, and will news that Dani and Roman have shared a little more than friendly advice destroy the chances of any reconciliation? After Jordan set Ella's heart ablaze with his vocals in the Dominican Republic, he has been prepping for his first date back in Essex with her ever since, but will Ella's commitment issues leave Jordan wishing that he had never bothered, or could this be the start of something special for the pair? After a heart-to-heart and getting everything off their chests in the Dom Rep, will Amy and Billy find it easy to get back on track and a slice of salsa dancing relight that spark for them, or will it create another opportunity for yet another argument? Finally, Brockett reflects that now might be time to let bygones be bygones with Saff... will she agree?

programme.title: Dawson's Creek
programme.desc: As he's forced to work on a rival's film, Dawson plots to record his own first kiss with Jen. Meanwhile, Joey misleads a wealthy suitor.

programme.title: Charmed

programme.title: Deal or No Deal

programme.title: The Floor US

programme.title: The Only Way is Essex
programme.desc: Reality series following the lives, loves and scandals of a group of real-life Essex guys and girls. Friction between the two big social groups in Essex is at an all-time high, and Junaid's frustration - particularly with Amber - is growing stronger by the day... after Courtney reaches out and invites Junaid to her birthday bash, will all be resolved over a slice of cake? Meanwhile, Ella and Jordan are fast becoming Essex's hot new couple, but Jordan is left wondering whether Ella has dropped him out completely after being blanked by her - will he be first to give her the cold shoulder, or will Ella beat him to the punch? Elsewhere, Gatsby and Dani are both keen to move on with their lives - but the explosions between them have made ripples in the different friendship groups and have created divides - and Amy decides to gather her pals and do a relationship round-up where they all unpack their issues.

programme.title: The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City
programme.desc: US reality series peeking inside the unconventional lives of six successful women living in or around Salt Lake City, Utah. At the end of the trip to Santorini, the women visit Angie's cousin at a winery, exploring family heritage. Later, they watch a Greek play about themselves by a local writer, causing disagreements among the group. The trip culminates in a dramatic final dinner where long-simmering conflicts erupt, and the women leave Greece with relationships forever changed.

programme.title: The Real Housewives of Orange County
programme.desc: Reality show following the lavish lifestyles of five 'housewives' and their families. programme.title: Celebrity Catchphrase
programme.desc: Stephen Mulhern hosts a celebrity special of the classic game show with Antony Cotton, Matt Dawson and Stacey Dooley all trying to 'say what they see' as they guess well-known phrases for the chance to win a 50,000-pound jackpot for their chosen charity.

programme.title: The Floor US

programme.title: The 1% Club
programme.desc: Have you ever wondered how clever you are? This is the quiz that the whole family can play together - 100 contestants begin every show and try to make it to the end to answer a question that only one per cent of the country can get right and win up to 100,000 pounds.

programme.title: Family Guy
